stage_1_draft.name: Draft
stage_1_draft.description: Author reads stem, choices, CorrectChoice, and existing ExplanationCorrect. Independently derives the correct answer per CAQS section 5.1. Verifies CorrectChoice matches. Then authors 1-3 distractor EW fields.
per_slot_requirements: Identify the specific error in THAT choice (not generic)
Name the misconception the candidate likely held
Reference the item actual topic or standard
stage_1_draft.quality_gate: G1 Draft Complete: All non-empty EW slots at 50 plus chars. No boilerplate. Each EW is choice-specific. EW[CorrectChoice] must be empty (DL-008 gate).
stage_1_draft.estimated_time: 5 min per distractor slot for MCQ. 10 min for case-study items. 15-25 min per item (MCQ: 3 distractors at 15 min; case: 3 distractors at 30 min).

stage_2_review.name: Review
stage_2_review.description: Peer review: second agent examines each item in the batch.
checks: Does each EW explain why THAT SPECIFIC CHOICE is wrong? (Not generic.)
Would a learner who selected this choice understand their error after reading the EW?
Is the accounting reasoning correct? Does it match ExplanationCorrect?
Are all CAQS section 4.2 element requirements satisfied? (why wrong, misconception, correction, surface plausibility)
No template or boilerplate text remains.
stage_2_review.quality_gate: G2 Peer Review PASS: All 5 checks satisfied. Failures return to Draft stage with specific item-level feedback.

stage_3_qa.name: Technical QA
stage_3_qa.description: Automated scan runs on the batch after Draft plus Review.
automated_checks: DL-008 scan: EW[CC] must be empty (Function-constructor parse, not regex window)
Empty-slot scan: EW[A-D] for non-CC positions must be non-empty (DL-026 gate)
Boilerplate scan: no placeholder or template patterns
Minimum-length scan: all EW slots at 50 plus chars
Governance guard Rule 2 check: no block-triggering violations
Parse-count check: item count unchanged (500 per pack)
stage_3_qa.quality_gate: G3 QA PASS: All automated checks pass. 0 errors, 0 warnings.

stage_4_certification_candidate.name: Certification Candidate
stage_4_certification_candidate.description: Item graduates from EW pipeline. EW fields are complete, QA-passed, and choice-specific. Item is ready for full CAQS section 1.6 six-dimension certification review in the 800-series pipeline.
stage_4_certification_candidate.handoff: EW Operating Model delivers items to the Certification Gateway. 800-series picks them up for correctness, precision, difficulty calibration, distractor engineering, blueprint alignment, and CMA Part 1 relevance verification.
stage_4_certification_candidate.quality_gate: G4 EW Complete: All 3 non-CC ExplanationWrong fields are non-empty, choice-specific, QA-passed. Item EW score: 10/10 on CAQS Dimension 7 (Explanation Quality).

Re-run DL-026 scan - verify 0 new empty non-CC slots.

ec_expansion_standard.structure: CAQS section 11.3 Mini-Lesson: (1) Concept Identification - name the governing principle or standard, (2) Solution Demonstration - formula to substitution to result to interpretation, (3) Error Analysis - why each distractor is wrong, what misconception each represents, (4) Business Application - what this means in practice, why a management accountant needs to know it, (5) Exam Preparation - common trap, related concepts, time management tip.
ec_expansion_standard.length: Minimum 500 chars. Target 800-1,200 chars for calculation items, 500-800 chars for conceptual items.

ew_replacement_standard.structure: Each distractor EW must: (1) Name the error type (calculation error, conceptual misapplication, standard confusion), (2) Show the exact wrong calculation path (for calculation items), (3) Contrast with the correct calculation path, (4) Identify the exam trap the distractor represents.
ew_replacement_standard.length: Minimum 80 chars (above CAQS 50-char minimum - boilerplate text is usually 150 plus chars but content-free).

rules: Do NOT alter stem or choices

agent_l_rewrite_operating_model.sequencing_dependency: EC expansion must come AFTER certification, not before. Rationale: if certification review discovers a CorrectChoice error (DL-030), the EC written for the wrong answer would need to be rewritten. Certification stabilizes the answer key, then EC expansion builds on stable foundation. This reverses the natural pipeline: certification first, then rewrite. This means the rewrite backlog grows during certification, and the rewrite phase is a second pass on already-certified items.

misconception_libraries.description: Catalog of common student errors mapped to specific distractor choices. Organized by topic (Revenue Recognition, Inventory, Variance Analysis, etc.).
misconception_libraries.velocity_impact: MODERATE. Author selects from a menu of common misconceptions rather than inventing from scratch. Reduces per-EW time from 5 min to approximately 3 min. Saves approximately 40 percent on the conceptual-analysis portion of EW authoring.
misconception_libraries.overhead: MEDIUM. Requires 1-2 sessions to build and maintain. Each topic area needs 5-15 misconceptions mapped. Risk: stale library leads to disuse.
misconception_libraries.recommendation: BUILD as part of EW Authoring Playbook. Not a separate lane - a reference appendix alongside the EW authoring process. Initial scope: top 10 topics by item count. Maintain organically.

distractor_libraries.description: Catalog of effective distractor patterns by topic. Example: variance analysis distractors - swaps actual and standard, omits quantity difference, doubles the rate difference, uses budget instead of flexible budget.
distractor_libraries.velocity_impact: LOW. Distractor patterns are inherently choice-specific - a library entry only helps if the current item distractor happens to match a cataloged pattern. The library helps train authors but does not directly speed authoring.
distractor_libraries.overhead: HIGH. Requires categorizing ALL distractors across 2,500 MCQs plus 420 case items. The catalog would be massive with low pattern-match rate.
distractor_libraries.recommendation: DO NOT BUILD as a standalone resource. Instead: integrate distractor patterns into the EW Authoring Playbook as worked examples (5-10 per topic area). Patterns are more useful as training material than as a reference library.

ew_templates.description: Standardized structures for common explanation types: Calculation Error EW, Conceptual Error EW, Misapplication EW. Fill-in templates that ensure CAQS section 4.2 compliance.
ew_templates.velocity_impact: HIGH. Templates eliminate structural framing overhead - author fills in the content, not the structure. Per-EW time drops from approximately 5 min to approximately 3 min (40 percent reduction). Templates ensure consistent quality.
ew_templates.overhead: LOW. One session to draft 3-4 templates. Near-zero maintenance overhead (templates do not go stale).
ew_templates.recommendation: BUILD IMMEDIATELY. This is the single highest-ROI standards artifact. 3-4 template stubs with CAQS section 4.2 fields as fill-in slots. Include 2 worked examples per template. Embed in EW Authoring Playbook.

explanation_templates.description: Mini-lesson structure templates for EC expansion per CAQS section 11.3: Concept Identification, Solution Demonstration, Error Analysis, Business Application, Exam Preparation. Standardized opening and closing conventions.
explanation_templates.velocity_impact: MODERATE. Templates reduce structural overhead for EC expansion but EC expansion is inherently content-heavy (800-1,200 chars) - the template only helps with the first and last 100 chars.
explanation_templates.overhead: LOW. Draft 1-2 templates. Include worked examples for calculation and conceptual item types.
explanation_templates.recommendation: BUILD as companion to EW templates. One session for both EW and EC templates. Include in EW Authoring Playbook.

net_velocity_assessment.total_investment: 2 sessions: Session 1 - EW templates (3-4) plus EC templates (1-2) plus worked examples. Session 2 - misconception library seed (top 10 topics, 5-15 misconceptions each).
net_velocity_assessment.total_return: 30-40 percent reduction in per-EW authoring time (5 min to 3-3.5 min). 20-30 percent reduction in per-EC expansion time. Extrapolated across 2,340 case EW slots plus approximately 500 MCQ EW slots equals approximately 2,840 slots. Time savings: approximately 95 hours to approximately 60 hours. At 2 batches per session equals approximately 12 sessions to approximately 8 sessions. Net: 4 sessions saved, 2 invested equals 2 sessions net gain.
net_velocity_assessment.vs_600_series: The 600-series proposal (3-4 session startup, 3-4 session savings) was DEFERRED by S309 because it was net-neutral. The Standards Library achieves the SAME net savings (4 sessions saved) with 50 percent of the startup investment (2 sessions) - and produces durable reference artifacts that outlive any single session series.
net_velocity_assessment.which_artifacts_are_overhead: Distractor libraries = DO NOT BUILD. Pattern-match rate too low, maintenance cost too high. Misconception libraries = BUILD the seed, let it grow organically. EW templates = BUILD immediately (highest ROI). EC templates = BUILD as companion. The distinction: templates (fill-in structure) equal velocity multiplier. Libraries (reference catalog) equal diminishing returns after seed.

agent_o_standards_library.recommendation: BUILD the Standards Library SEED (2 sessions) as pre-work to the 800-series certification waves. Do NOT launch a 600-series lane. The seed consists of: (a) EW Authoring Playbook (1-page process reference plus 3-4 EW templates with worked examples), (b) EC Expansion Playbook (1-2 templates with worked examples), (c) Misconception Library seed (top 10 topics, 50-150 misconceptions). These are reference artifacts, not infrastructure. They accelerate the EW and EC authoring tasks that are already part of the 800-series certification pipeline.

consolidated_session_724_recommendation.decision: DO NOT LAUNCH 600-series Content Operations and Authoring Infrastructure lane.
rationale: S309 deferral is CONFIRMED by this session deeper analysis across 5 agents.
The binding constraint is AUTHOR CAPACITY (human cognitive time to write choice-specific explanations), and no infrastructure lane can solve that constraint.
The existing 800-series certification pipeline with HYBRID strategy already embeds EW authoring and EC expansion.
The 600-series concept was net-neutral at best (3-4 sessions invested for 3-4 sessions saved per S309).
A lightweight EW Authoring Playbook achieves the same velocity improvement (approximately 40 percent) at 50 percent of the startup cost (2 sessions vs. 4 sessions).
recommended_actions: Create EW Authoring Playbook as a lightweight reference (1 session, includes templates plus misconception seed) - this is the 600-series MVP without the infrastructure overhead.
Embed EW authoring and EC expansion into existing 800-series certification waves (already the HYBRID strategy, no change required).
Distinguish genuine rewrites (approximately 330 items needing content creation) from label-edits (approximately 920 items needing metadata-only changes). Use correct scope for resource estimation.
Prioritize case-bank EW authoring (310 Certified items, target 80 percent fill) as the single highest-ROI activity for learner experience improvement.
Adopt the 4-stage EW operating model from Agent K (Draft, Review, QA, Certification Candidate) as the standard process embedded in every certification batch.
Create the Standards Library seed as pre-work (EW templates, EC templates, misconception library seed) in 2 sessions before 800-series certification waves begin.
consolidated_session_724_recommendation.verdict: The 600-series concept was a reasonable exploration, but the S307-S309 analytics pipeline, S723 governance closure, and this S724 strategy session collectively demonstrate that the existing governance infrastructure is sufficient. The task is EXECUTION, not reorganization. The gap between current state (2,181 Certified, 2,403 missing EW slots) and target state (2,500 Certified, 80 percent EW fill) is addressable within the existing 800-series certification framework. No new lane is required.
